description: Performs repeated DNS A-record lookups for sequentially generated subdomains using the Winsock getaddrinfo API. Each query uses a counter-based hostname format under a controlled lab domain and is separated by a fixed sleep interval.

dns_beacon_client.role: generates sequential DNS hostnames and resolves them using getaddrinfo to create observable DNS beacon traffic

dns_server.role: responds to generated DNS A-record lookups for the controlled lab domain

beacon_behavior.description: The sample builds sequential DNS query names, performs IPv4 A-record resolution using getaddrinfo, logs whether each query resolved, sleeps for a fixed interval, and repeats for a fixed number of iterations.
expected_actions: generate sequential query names using tick-#### format
perform IPv4 DNS lookup using getaddrinfo
free DNS resolution results using freeaddrinfo

code_placement: DNS beaconing logic is implemented directly inside the native C++ executable using Winsock resolver APIs
execution_trigger: Program entry point starts the DNS beacon loop automatically
execution_target: controlled DNS domain beacon01.lab.local resolved by the lab DNS server

dns_beacon_client: freeaddrinfo usage to release resolver results
std::setw and std::setfill usage for zero-padded counter formatting
AF_INET hint restricting resolution to IPv4 A-record behavior
absence of HTTP or HTTPS client logic

network: outbound DNS A-record queries for beacon01.lab.local subdomains
query counter increases sequentially from tick-0001 through tick-0010
DNS responses resolve to the controlled lab IP address when INetSim DNS is configured
approximately 15 second interval between DNS queries
no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required for this sample
no TCP command channel is established
process: A05_2a_dns_beacon.exe runs as a standalone process
no downloaded payload is written to disk
host: console output shows DNS beacon startup
console output shows configured base domain
console output logs each generated query
console output reports whether each query resolved
program exits after completing all iterations

semantic_meaning: Demonstrates a controlled DNS beaconing pattern in which a program periodically generates unique subdomain lookups under a lab-controlled domain, using DNS resolution itself as the observable signaling mechanism rather than HTTP requests, payload downloads, or interactive command channels.

control_notes.payload_effect: generates observable DNS beacon traffic only

success_conditions: Windows VM is configured to use the controlled lab DNS server
controlled DNS server resolves generated beacon01.lab.local subdomains
sample performs DNS lookups using getaddrinfo
console output reports resolved or not resolved status for each query
INetSim service.log records DNS A-record queries
PCAP captures show sequential DNS queries
approximately 10 DNS beacon queries are observed
queries occur at approximately 15 second intervals
program exits after completing all iterations
